masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: PTC Industries: a wealth-creation engine putting India on the global aerospace-titanium map.

subhead.text: A 62-year-old Lucknow foundry, now Safran's titanium casting supplier for the LEAP jet engine, building India's first advanced vacuum-arc-remelt titanium facility.

p1_engine.eyebrow: A wealth-creation engine, still reinvesting harder than it distributes

blocks.text: Revenue nearly doubled in the latest year alone (TTM growth ~96%, ₹257 Cr to ₹603 Cr over three years), PAT grew from ₹42 Cr to ₹102 Cr over the same stretch, and the 5-year trend is even sharper — ~30% revenue CAGR, ~101% profit CAGR. Market cap sits at ₹26,869 Cr, a scale disproportionate to current revenue, reflecting the market's own read on the growth trajectory.

ROE (7%) and ROCE (8.43%) are modest relative to that growth — a company-level figure that reflects heavy, ongoing capex (a ₹1,000 crore program at Lucknow, described as fully funded) diluting near-term returns rather than weak underlying profitability.

In November 2023 it signed a multi-year contract with Safran Aircraft Engines to supply titanium casting parts for the CFM LEAP engine (the engine powering single-aisle jets like the Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX family) — a genuinely tier-one global aerospace OEM relationship, not a domestic-only story.

Domestic defense momentum is building fast alongside the export story: a ₹110 Cr order from BrahMos Aerospace (August 2025) and, in 2026, an order from ISRO's VSSC for double-VAR-melted aerospace-grade titanium ingots — plus subsidiary Aerolloy Technologies commissioning a Vacuum Arc Remelting furnace (1,500 MT/year capacity) and a 600-tonne plasma arc melting furnace, building an integrated titanium production chain that PTC itself frames as putting India on the global aerospace-titanium map.

It holds AS9100, NADCAP special-process accreditation, DGQA Ministry of Defence approval, and marine classification approvals from Bureau Veritas, DNV GL, Lloyd's Register, ABS and RINA — a genuinely broad certification spread across aerospace, defense and industrial end-markets, plus a DSIR-recognized R&D lab behind its own licensed technologies (Replicast®, Rapidcast™, Forgecast™).

insights.point: The field is **growing fast, and global capacity is genuinely constrained right now.**
insights.evidence: Aerospace titanium market: $4.1-4.5B (2022-25) to $4-7B by 2030-2035, 5.3-9.0%/yr. Precision Castparts (Berkshire Hathaway) committed over $628 million in new capacity, including a $500 million titanium melt facility, direct evidence of a global capacity squeeze tied to Boeing/Airbus production ramps.

insights.point: **NADCAP/AS9100 certification is the actual competitive gate**, and PTC already clears it.
insights.evidence: NADCAP lets OEMs/Tier-1s fast-track supplier audits, cutting weeks-to-months out of new-supplier qualification — PTC's certification spread (including DGQA Green Channel Status) puts it inside that pre-validated circle already.

insights.point: Listed Indian peers show **a wide range of outcomes even within the same niche.**
insights.evidence: MTAR Technologies posts a steadier 13% ROE at ₹876 Cr revenue; Azad Engineering, closer to PTC's own growth profile, saw ROE fall from 9.1% to 6.2% as heavy capacity capex weighed on returns — the same dynamic visible in PTC's own modest ROE despite explosive revenue growth.

insights.point: Management guidance itself frames this as a **multi-year scale-up, not a one-off contract win.**
insights.evidence: Guidance points to 90-100% revenue growth in FY26 and a target of 10-15x revenue growth over the next 5-7 years — an aggressive, publicly-stated trajectory, not a conservative baseline.

reflect.text: A 62-year-old foundry that just became India's entry point into a globally capacity-constrained aerospace-titanium market, growing revenue and profit at rates most Indian industrials never reach. The modest ROE isn't weakness — it's the visible cost of reinvesting into that position faster than most companies would dare.

p3_opportunities.lede: One place worth watching, already funded and named directly in the company's own gap research.

items.title: Scaling the Mehsana (Gujarat) facility for global supply chain capture
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research names this directly: PTC is increasing capacity multiple times over the next few years at its Gujarat facility with advanced manufacturing equipment, robotic systems and automated fettling technologies — specifically to capture global supply-chain realignment as manufacturers diversify away from concentrated sourcing.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only PTC Industries' own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Track ROE/ROCE recovery as the Lucknow and Mehsana capex programs complete
items.body: Since the current modest ROE looks capex-driven rather than structural, track it specifically as the ₹1,000 Cr Lucknow program and Mehsana expansion move from build-out to full utilization, to confirm the returns actually follow the revenue growth.

intro.text: A workflow is the set of steps a company runs to get a result. Below are the generic steps for an aerospace/industrial titanium casting manufacturer in this segment — a directory-depth pass, not yet confirmed against PTC's own stated process, so marked generic throughout.

steps: offer investment-cast and forged titanium/superalloy structural and rotating components
serve aero-engine, airframe, and defense/industrial applications
win named OEM programs (e.g. LEAP engine casting parts)

takeaway.text: Sixty-two years of foundry heritage just turned into a Safran LEAP engine contract and India's own advanced titanium VAR facility. The modest ROE is the **visible cost of building the next decade, not a sign it isn't working.**
